clue.text: Square or circle concealed in coat

indicators.note: the circle is hidden away within the coat, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an animal's coat is its fur
O is the round, circle-shaped letter

explanation.surface: A shape, square or round, tucked away inside someone's overcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Two squared makes this number, and a four-square thing has four equal sides, so the number is a fair sense of square.

clue.text: Reject recording, having left before end

indicators.note: the left-hand letter comes ahead of the end in the answer

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record or CD, a recording
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a record, having walked out before it finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclaim is to deny or renounce, which is to reject a claim or responsibility.

clue.text: River animal surfacing, finishing on the road?

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up to the surface means reading from the bottom upwards, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
a rat is an animal

explanation.surface: A river creature comes up for air and ends up on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surfacing' turns CAMRAT into the answer; it also hints at the road surface itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The material is the final surface laid on a road, its finish, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Jazz musician renders number with one in support

parts.note: to count is to number, and a count is a number

indicators.note: the one is placed within the support

parts.note: a base is a support or foundation
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A jazz player performs a number while one person backs him up.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Basie was a celebrated American jazz pianist and big-band leader.

clue.text: Catholic about to be presented with willow staff for bishop

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the abbreviation for Catholic is read backwards

parts.note: RC is short for Roman Catholic
an osier is a kind of willow used in basketry

explanation.surface: A Catholic is about to be handed a willow stick to give a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: The hooked staff carried by a bishop as a sign of office is called a crozier.

clue.text: Lady's companion with affection not very little

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the abbreviation for very from the affection word

parts.note: love is affection
V is the small abbreviation of very

explanation.surface: A lady's companion shows affection that is far from small.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s' is read as 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so it fairly stands for a lady.

clue.text: Leftie is given commendations for what he does in Robin-Hood act?

definitions.text: what he does in Robin-Hood act?

parts.note: a red is a left-winger or communist
tributes are words of praise, commendations

explanation.surface: A left-winger gets praised for playing Robin Hood.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood took from the rich and gave to the poor, sharing wealth out differently, which is what this verb describes.

clue.text: Endorse party that gets stuck in ready to learn

indicators.note: the party is lodged inside the other word, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: apt means quick or ready to learn
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Backing a political party that sets to work, keen to learn.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt a proposal is to accept and approve it, so it means endorse.

clue.text: Cut charge for framing painting showing prince

indicators.note: framing means the shortened charge surrounds the painting like a picture frame
cut tells us to lop the last letter off the word for charge

parts.note: something in your charge is in your trust
oil is an oil painting

explanation.surface: An art dealer lowers his fee for framing a portrait of royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like an adjective on the charge but is the trimming signal, and 'framing' plays on the painting picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Troilus was a Trojan prince, son of King Priam, famed from Chaucer and Shakespeare.

clue.text: Minister clever but not always? Fine!

indicators.note: but not means the word for always is taken away from clever

parts.note: ever means always
an eric is an old Irish fine paid as blood money by a killer to the victim's kin

explanation.surface: A government minister is clever, though not all the time; very well, then!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine!' looks like an exclamation of agreement, but it is a noun: the eric, a fine in old Irish law.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman is a minister of religion, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Academic garaging old car in Canada once?

indicators.note: a garage holds a car inside it, so the academic surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A university lecturer keeps an old car locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada was formally styled a self-governing territory of the British Empire from 1867, an example of this status.

clue.text: Like style of art somehow so clean and so 'Latin'?

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are arranged in some fresh way

parts.note: sic is the Latin word for so or thus

explanation.surface: Asking about an artistic style that is tidy and Latin-flavoured.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes art reviving the forms of ancient Greece and Rome, an adjective for a style.

clue.text: Journalist, I cited Tory being corrupt

indicators.note: corrupt suggests something spoiled or altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaperman reports that he named a Tory as corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the newspaper editor in charge of financial news, a kind of journalist.

clue.text: Type born at the outset to be cheat

indicators.note: at the outset picks the opening letter of the word born, which leads the answer

parts.note: ilk means type or kind

explanation.surface: Someone is a born swindler from the very start.
explanation.definitionFit: To bilk someone is to swindle or defraud them, a synonym of cheat.

clue.text: Shame impostor is wicked — complete conversion needed

indicators.note: wicked suggests something twisted or bent out of shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A wicked fraud must be utterly reformed.
explanation.definitionFit: A total change of form, as caterpillar to butterfly, is a complete transformation.

clue.text: Disease that could create lameness, knocking out any number

indicators.note: could create says the remaining letters can be reworked into something new
knocking out says one letter is removed from the word lameness

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: An illness that might leave someone lame, knocking them out.
explanation.definitionFit: An infectious viral illness with a red rash, a classic disease of childhood.

clue.text: Front of hotel priest has left — place to fly away from

indicators.note: front of means only the first letter of hotel is used

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A priest has checked out from in front of the hotel to catch a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing pad for helicopters is a place from which one can take off and fly.

clue.text: Note, note, note

parts.note: fa is a note in tonic sol-fa
me is another note in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: Just the same word three times, as if jotting a reminder.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of note has renown, so note in that sense is celebrity.

clue.text: Officers change name in requirement for membership

indicators.note: the change and name are put inside the membership word

parts.note: subs are membership fees for a club
to alter is to change

explanation.surface: Army officers rewrite a name in the club's entry rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Junior army officers below captain are known by this rank title.

clue.text: In short second year gets lean, thin

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, the shortened form being signalled by in short
to cant is to lean or tilt

explanation.surface: Briefly, by the second year someone has grown lean and thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty means meagre or barely enough, so a thin supply or garment.

clue.text: Quick half-century, new opener

indicators.note: opener points to the first letter, which is swapped for the new one

parts.note: fifty is half of a hundred, a half-century in cricket

explanation.surface: A batsman scores a quick fifty as a new opening bat.
explanation.walkthrough: A half-century is fifty runs in cricket, the bat-and-ball game; the cricket picture hides the letter swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Nifty means nimble or speedy, so it can stand for quick.

clue.text: Legal petitioner's humbug, left with ambition squashed

indicators.note: the left and ambition are squashed into the middle of the humbug word

parts.note: cant is hypocritical talk, humbug
an aim is an ambition

explanation.surface: A litigant talks hypocrisy after his ambitions are crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s' is read as 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: One who makes a claim in court is a party petitioning the law for something.

clue.text: Diverted at Oxford? The reverse by Bullingdon Club type!

indicators.note: the reverse tells us to read the university word backwards

parts.note: a student in residence at university is said to be up
a toff is an upper-class person, the sort in Oxford's exclusive Bullingdon Club

explanation.surface: A posh Oxford student is sent off course by a Bullingdon Club member.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bullingdon Club is an exclusive, rowdy Oxford dining club for wealthy students.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put off is to be distracted or deflected from one's purpose, so diverted.

clue.text: Be fruitful as side, according to report

indicators.note: according to report means the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A side is told it must be productive.
explanation.definitionFit: To teem is to be full or abundant, an old sense being to bear offspring.

clue.text: Son — someone funny or a pain?

parts.note: a hoot is an amusing person

explanation.surface: Is a son an entertainer or a nuisance?
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden stab of discomfort can be described by this noun, as in a shooting pain.

clue.text: Operations in sudden move forward, taking line

parts.note: a surge is a sudden forward rush
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Military operations are part of a sudden push forward along a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery means surgical operations collectively, the work done on patients.
